files.notes/close_checklist.md:
# June 2026 close — controller checklist

Owner: B. Okafor. Complete sequentially; no skipping ahead.

1. Reconcile operating cash to the June bank statement. For every book-side item identified by the reconciliation, prepare one correcting journal entry per item.
2. Review the payroll register for any pay period ending after 6/30 that pays in July. If such a period exists, accrue the full gross wages to Accrued Liabilities; note that in some months every payroll run pays in-month.
3. Confirm June prepaid amortization against the prepaid schedule, supporting contracts, and the GL. If it is not already recorded, book June amortization as ONE combined journal entry—do not duplicate an existing entry. Apply the convention that a full month is taken in the month an item begins.
4. Book June depreciation per the fixed asset register, after checking the GL to confirm it has not already been posted.
5. Test June vendor-bill expense coding by comparing the bill documents with the GL. Reclass anything miscoded to the correct expense account.
6. Prepare June budget-vs-actual variance commentary on an as-closed basis, only after items 1-5 have been booked.
files.notes/company_background.md:
# Company background

Lakeside Family Health LLC began when a small group of primary-care clinicians saw a practical gap in their community: patients wanted a clinic that felt personal, but employers and local organizations also needed dependable access to routine health services. The founders built the practice around straightforward scheduling, familiar faces, and clear follow-up rather than a large-system atmosphere.

Today, Lakeside Family Health LLC provides primary-care visits, preventive care, basic wellness services, occupational health consultations, and coordinated clinic programs for business customers. Its work combines direct patient care with employer-sponsored services, allowing the clinic to support both individuals and local teams.

The staff has the character of a close-knit neighborhood practice. Clinicians tend to know returning patients by name, the front desk keeps the day moving with good humor, and the operations team is quietly particular about records, authorizations, and follow-through. Outside specialists and service vendors supplement the core team where needed.

The current focus is steady execution: maintaining service quality, keeping business records current, and balancing patient demand with the administrative needs of a growing clinic. Leadership is also refining outreach to local employers and community partners while preserving the approachable style that shaped the practice in the first place.
files.notes/marketing_plan_h2.md:
# H2 marketing plan — working draft

## What we want to accomplish

- Refresh the Lakeside Family Health LLC brand without losing the warm, neighborhood-clinic feel.
- Improve awareness of primary care, preventive visits, and workplace health services.
- Build a repeatable referral path with employers and community organizations.
- Host two educational webinars per quarter.

## Priority audiences

- Families and adults looking for an accessible primary-care relationship
- Local employers seeking practical workplace health support
- Community partners whose clients need a trusted clinic referral

## Planned work

**Brand refresh:** Tighten the visual system, simplify service descriptions, and update core website and handout language.

**Educational content:** Develop plain-language webinar topics around preventive care, workplace wellness, and preparing for routine visits. Reuse each session as short articles and social posts.

**Partner pilot:** Test a co-marketing program with a small group of aligned local organizations. Provide ready-to-share copy, referral guidance, and a simple contact route.

**Patient communications:** Use friendly reminders and service spotlights, with an emphasis on usefulness rather than sales language.

## Measurement

Track inquiries, appointment requests, webinar attendance, partner referrals, and engagement with refreshed service pages. Review results at the end of each quarter and adjust the channel mix. Final scope remains subject to the Q2 close.
files.notes/prior_accountant_memo.md:
# Notes from the old desk

B. Okafor — a few things that will save you some hunting:

- The bank tends to add its own fees and service charges near the end of the statement. Those usually are not in the books yet; our practice has been to pick them up during close.
- June moved fast, and I would not trust every vendor bill to have landed in the right expense account. Use the source documents in `bills/` as authoritative and correct the coding where needed.
- The budget was locked early in Q2. The one-off June work came later and was never planned, so those items should explain most of the larger budget-to-actual variances.
- One payroll timing item matters this month: the June 16-30 payroll run does not pay until the first days of July. The payroll register has the support.

— Prior staff accountant
